name: Opus Broadening
strategy: Broadening expressed where it is actually paying: an equal-weight and free-cash-flow value core, an AI-capex industrial sleeve, a regional-bank curve steepener, healthcare as the defensive broadening leader, energy at a residual weight, and the gold hedge retired into a larger cash buffer that now out-yields it in a hiking regime.
reassessment_note: One change: GLD (6%) is closed into cash; every other leg is unchanged at the same weight and the same stop and take-profit levels. What I checked: Yahoo daily closes through 11-13 plus news searches. October CPI came in at +0.4% m/m against a 0.3% consensus on 11-10. CME FedWatch now fully prices a 25bp December hike, with roughly 10% odds of 50bp, and Logan is calling for at least two hikes. The 10-year is back at 5.15% (from 4.86% on 11-09), the 30-year is at 5.48%, 3-month bills are at 4.12% and DXY is at a three-month high of 103.4. Gold futures fell from $4,114 to $3,886 and GLD is -6.3% on the leg, 3.7 points from its stop. A non-yielding hedge facing hikes, rising real yields and a firm dollar costs too much to carry. Cash at 4% APY now does the defensive job better and with no mark-to-market risk, so I take the loss now rather than wait for the -10% stop. The rest of the book is working or flat. XLE is +4.9% as WTI holds in the high $80s. COWZ, RSP and XLV are slightly positive, and XLI and KRE are within 1% of entry. A steeper 10y-3m curve (about 103bp) supports the KRE steepener thesis, so I do not churn those legs. Research was limited: the search index returned few dated items for this week, and I relied on fetched price series and a handful of 11-03 to 11-10 news reports.

positions.thesis: Free-cash-flow value core (+0.9% on the leg). Cash-generative, low-multiple companies hold up better than long-duration growth when the 10-year is back above 5% and the Fed is pricing hikes. This is the largest leg because it is the cleanest expression of broadening that does not rely on falling rates.

Equal-weight S&P 500 is the mandate's core broadening exposure. It is flat on the leg (+0.1%) while SPY chops, and it lowers the book's exposure to mega-cap concentration. Unchanged size, with a 10% stop as the risk cap.

Residual energy weight, +4.9% on the leg as WTI firmed from $86 to $88.6. It is the book's inflation-surprise hedge now that gold is gone: a hot CPI print is better hedged by energy cash flows than by bullion. Kept at 8% rather than raised because crude is still well below its October highs near $98.

AI-capex and reshoring industrial sleeve, flat on the leg (-0.1%) after rebounding from 162.7 on 11-06. Data-center power and electrical buildout spending is not sensitive to a 25bp hike. Holding the 10% size; the stop sits below the early-November low.

Regional-bank curve steepener. The 10y-3m spread has widened to about 103bp (5.15% vs 4.12%) as long yields rose faster than bills this week, which supports net interest margins. Down 1% on the leg; the thesis is intact, and the 14% stop allows for credit-headline volatility.

Healthcare as the defensive broadening leader, up from 167 in mid-August to 188.9 and holding gains (+0.3% on the leg). It is low-beta, earnings-driven exposure that does not depend on the rate path, and it is the book's equity defense now that GLD is out.
